1. **List.** Run `scripts/select-plans.py --working <working>`; it keeps
   only `planning_ready` plans (dependencies available) outside dependency
   cycles, backlog first.
   - `implementation_ready: false`: keep it selectable, report the blocker,
     and do not dispatch implementation until its start or resume check passes.
   - `degraded: true`: report the selector error, list `<working>/plans/`
     for the user, and stop.
2. **Report.** Report `excluded_by_dependency`. If `plans` is empty, say
   `No backlog or active plans available. Nothing to run.` and stop.
3. **Present.** Present each option as `<id> - <title>`.

## Dispatch tasks

Read `references/orchestration.md` for posture, cap, and briefs.

### Check drift once

Before the first wave, if files in the plan's scope changed since the plan
was written (`git log --oneline -- <paths>`), re-check affected tasks before
dispatch.

### Choose the next wave

1. Before each wave, run `varde work execution-wave --repo-root
   <checkout> <plan-dir> --json` and report `data.blocked_by_dep`,
   `data.reasons`, and `data.wave_mode`. Exit 3 is a dependency cycle, a
   hard failure.
2. Run any subset of `data.next_wave` together, never more: never combine tasks
   from different resolver runs or pair tasks named in `data.conflicts`.

### Choose a strategy

| Strategy | Use when | Who executes |
|---|---|---|
| `parallel` | `execution=auto` (the default) and `next_wave` holds two or more tasks | one background builder per fresh task worktree |
| `serial` | `execution=serial`, or auto with one task | one background builder at a time in a fresh task worktree |
| `inline` | `execution=inline`, or no builder is available | the current agent, one fresh task worktree at a time |

Announce each wave's strategy and task ids. Use
`references/build-parallel.md` for wave isolation and integration, including a
one-task serial or inline wave.

### Task-file ownership

The orchestrator alone edits plan/task state in the plan approval checkout.
Builders read their supplied task context, edit only their bound source
scope, and return evidence and commits from their task worktrees. Register
bindings per `references/build-worktree.md` before dispatch.

### Dispatch a builder

Move a task whose `kind` is set to anything but `research` to `blocked`
with reason `<kind> tasks are no longer supported; resolve the question in
planning`.

1. Obtain any missing pre-edit verdict per `references/review-gates.md`;
   material drift returns to that gate.
2. Move the task to `in_progress` (`varde work transition <task.md>
   in_progress --json`; legal from `todo` or `blocked`). A corrective
   re-dispatch of a task already `in_progress` skips this step.
3. Brief the builder with:
   - the task file path and posture (`plan-execution` | `debug` |
     `refactor`);
   - its `#### Verification` checks, `modifies`/`creates`/`renames` paths, and
     `verification_resources`;
   - the task's scope and `#### Out of scope` text and the plan context it
     needs, quoted, so the builder never opens `plan.md`;
   - the execution location and bounded context;
   - the plan's review subject id and the resolved absolute `<working>` and
     `<knowledge>` paths, used without re-resolving;
   - the independent pre-edit verdict, approved verification approach, and any
     pending aggregate implementation review;
   - `references/build-execution.md`, read before its first tool call.

After each wave, regenerate listed outputs through an owned writing-task
worktree and integrate their verified commit before starting dependents.

### Accept a result

- When a builder returns `blocked` or reports a failed attempt, read
  `references/build-recovery.md` and follow its retry and blocked-task rules.
- Before accepting a completed implementation task, compare its commit with
  the task's declared paths: `varde work check-task-ownership --task
  <task.md> --commit <task-commit> --json`. When `data.status` is `stray` (exit 2), re-dispatch once
  with `data.stray`, counting toward the bounded retry in
  `references/build-recovery.md` (read it before that re-dispatch); `skipped`
  needs no action. The corrective builder amends the task commit only when
  `git rev-parse HEAD` in its execution branch equals that commit, else
  reports `blocked`; rerun the ownership check on the new SHA it reports.
  Accept the task only after the scope is corrected and its source is
  verified and published to the plan branch.

Accepting any task moves it to `done` and commits its task file when plan
storage is tracked; release its binding before starting dependents.

### Review checkpoints

Tasks inherit the plan's subject; never initialize one per task. Check `start`
before moving a backlog or blocked plan, or a task, into implementation, and
`resume` before continuing an active plan or interrupted task:

```sh
varde work review check --subject <subject-id> --checkpoint start --json
varde work review check --subject <subject-id> --checkpoint resume --json
```

- A typed review blocker holds implementation until reviewer evidence is
  resolved or refreshed; it is not a dependency result.
=== skills/varde-change/references/orchestrate.md ===
# Orchestrate mode

Run a group plan's children end to end. Children are nested `plan.md`s; id
`<group-id>/<child-slug>`. The orchestrator never edits production source or
dispatches tasks.

## Route

| The request is | Action |
|---|---|
| Names a group plan | Go to **Order children**. |
| Requests a whole feature without naming a group | **Discover groups**. |
| Names a plan without `shape: group` | Build plan `<id>` (`varde-change build`, named-plan route) and stop. |

## Discover groups

1. Read `<working>/plans/*/plan.md` frontmatter; keep `shape: group` plans with
   at least one non-`completed` child.
2. Present each as `<group-id> — <title>`. If none qualify, report
   `No group plans with unbuilt children. Nothing to orchestrate.`
3. Stop until the user selects one.

## Order children

1. Run `varde work readiness` on each child and order by
   `data.planning_ready` and dependency blockers; leave review blockers to the
   child build. `depends_on` holds sibling slugs only.
2. Skip completed children; completed dependencies are satisfied.
3. A missing dependency blocks its child; a cycle stops the feature. Report
   blockers before any child runs.
4. Establish or recover the visible group plan approval worktree per
   [Feature worktree](#feature-worktree).

## Feature worktree

Use a stable group plan worktree regardless of plan storage location.

1. Load `references/build-worktree.md` and use id `orchestrate-<group-id>` for
   plan bootstrap and prerequisite checkpoints. Validate any caller-owned reused
   path/branch before entering it; writing tasks require the clean plan commit.
2. Map group, child, and task paths to their physical copies in the feature
   checkout. Pass those explicit (mapped) paths and the resolved absolute
   `<working>` and `<knowledge>` paths.

That checkout is the owning approval repository for group and child subjects:
initialize and independently review exact-root subjects there; never copy
main-checkout approvals. Serial
children finish their local gates and tracked state in that checkout, so
completed dependencies unlock later children. Every child writing task uses a
fresh separate task worktree; dependent tasks start from verified plan commits.
Expose the group path, branch/base, and short status for IDE/Git review.

## Approve and activate the group

1. Read the group and every child contract. Confirm the group's aggregate
   source scope, child IDs/dependencies/contracts, assumptions, and
   acceptance/verification outside Progress match them. Material drift
   updates that contract and needs fresh independent approval before any child
   runs.
2. Use the exact-root group subject initialized and approved at plan
   finalization (id in Progress). A recovered different approval root needs its
   own initialization and review; never copy or reset approvals. Each child
   keeps its own subject and gates; group approval does not replace them.
3. Run `review check --subject <group-subject-id> --checkpoint start --json`;
   a blocker stops before child execution. Transition a backlog or blocked
   group to active; an active group stays active.
4. Commit the activation when plan storage is tracked.

## Delegate children

Run the remaining children sequentially in dependency order, waiting for each
result: build plan `<compound-child-id>` (`varde-change build`, named-plan
route) in the feature location. Give each child the resolved absolute
`<working>` and `<knowledge>` paths; it uses them without re-resolving. Build
owns single-plan execution and review in that approval checkout, with fresh
worktrees for writers and local integration back to its authorized plan branch.
It leaves final user target integration to the group owner.

When a child blocks or fails, stop immediately: run no later child, merge
nothing, leave commits and partial state as they are, and report the failed
child, the reason, and the completed children.

## Resume

1. Recover any existing feature location, derive progress from child statuses,
   and resume at the first non-`completed` child.
2. On `worktree-create.sh` exit 3, inspect `git worktree list --porcelain`.
   Reuse `.varde/worktrees/orchestrate-<group-id>` only when that path is
   registered with branch `worktree/orchestrate-<group-id>`. A branch-only
   collision or a missing or mismatched worktree stops recovery.
3. Stop when statuses and commits disagree, such as a completed child without
   commits.

## Finish

1. **Release nested bindings.** A live nested task binding must be integrated
   and released at its owning approval checkout before group completion.
2. **Review the group.** After all children are completed:
   1. Verify the aggregate acceptance criteria and combined behavior.
   2. Obtain an independent entire-group implementation review of
      integration evidence only (group subject, aggregate contract and
      criteria, child results, cross-child interfaces; no
      child implementation details), recording current
      entire-subject evidence per `references/review-gates.md`; child reviews
      and the contract-drift check stand.
   3. Route its findings through `varde-review` fix.md's Fix loop (build
      mode, no combined triage table); make source, spec, and documentation
      edits through bounded `varde-change` builds, then run checks and refresh
      the group evidence.
3. **Escalate deferred findings.** Run
   `varde work escalate-deferred --plan-dir <group-plan-dir>
   --deferred-dir <working>/reviews/deferred` (absolute paths; safe to rerun)
   and report its lines. This copies group
   action items (blank findings with an `**Escalated:** scope-creep` note)
   to deferred review. Fix malformed findings before retrying; recover an
   interrupted transaction with `varde work recover` before rerunning.
4. **Conclude.** Run `varde work review check --subject
   <group-subject-id> --checkpoint complete --json`, then `varde work
   conclude <group-plan.md> --json`. Missing/stale approval or an incomplete
   child blocks conclusion: preserve the active group and recovery refs, and
   never mark it completed by a plain transition or activate it again. A
   feature checkout owning the group subject may conclude against verified
   local source; never conclude a main-checkout subject against unmerged
   feature source.
5. **Commit.** At the owning checkout, commit tracked group conclusion and
   bookkeeping before offering Merge or Push, staging only this group's
   verified paths and preserving unrelated edits.
6. **Offer one choice.** Give the clickable group worktree path, branch/base,
   short checks, and concerns for IDE/Git review, without pasting the diff.
   Offer the group's applicable target-integration choices per
   `references/build-finish.md`'s Finish choices, and execute only the
   one the user makes.
7. **Reflect.** Invoke `varde-knowledge reflect` as a session boundary (child
   builds already recorded their own lessons); it writes a feature-level
   handoff when anything is left for later.
=== skills/varde-change/references/orchestration.md ===
# Orchestration

The main agent orchestrates and stays available to the user. Delegate bounded
work to background `varde-*` agents.

## Cap

- At most `[orchestration] max_agents` subagents in flight (the installed
  instruction block shows the active value). `varde-explorer` runs do not count.
- `varde-explorer` never spawns.

## Pre-explore

Only OpenCode and Pi (which needs pi-subagents) let planners, builders, and
reviewers spawn `varde-explorer` and nothing else; on other harnesses they
spawn nothing.

On other harnesses, before dispatching a planner, builder, or reviewer:

1. Run up to 2 `varde-explorer` over the task's owned and affected areas.
2. Put their notes in the brief.

The subagent uses the `varde-explore` skill only for gaps.

## Brief

When `varde` is installed, run `varde setup watch --ensure --repo
<repo-root>` before the first dispatch, retrying once with escalated access;
sandboxed subagents cannot start it.

### Writer launch

Before dispatching a writer, resolve the permission manifest and launch
contract in `references/build-worktree.md`. Supply its exact cwd and session
permissions through a supported launcher; if unavailable, report the limit
before launch. Require the worker's actual-sandbox preflight before edits.
A parent-side probe cannot establish the worker's permissions.

### Brief contents

Each brief gives one bounded task and:

- file ownership;
- orientation: files and line ranges you read, key symbols, decisions made,
  and exact check commands, seeded from `varde map context_pack` minus
  unrelated hits;
- resolved `<working>` and `<knowledge>` paths;
- the spawn rule: explorers only, up to 2, or none;
- "Do the work yourself; do not launch other subagents."

## Results

- Review each result before integrating it.
- Builders run lint and their task checks. The orchestrator runs reviews and
  full suites.
=== skills/varde-change/references/plan-decomposition.md ===
# Task decomposition

Break a settled spec and its plan-level acceptance criteria (`plan.md`, or the
minimal plan synthesized for ad-hoc work) into `tasks/<task-id>.md` files from
`assets/TASK-TEMPLATE.md`. Run once while finalizing a plan, or at build for
an ad-hoc plan without tasks; a single bounded outcome writes one task directly from that template instead
(plan AC → its Verification), skipping the edge-case checks below.

## 1. Check the edge cases

Check these:

| The goal | Decompose as |
|---|---|
| Names a shared symbol, type, or interface (with `varde map`, run `symbol_blast_radius` rather than guessing from package structure) | Wide refactor: expand, N migrate batches, contract, plus an integrate task if batches can't stay green |
| Deletes a generated or intermediate file another task may read | Deletion: grep draft task bodies for the path, tests for hardcoded paths under the deleted dir, and dependents/importers of the deleted source |
| Creates or renames a path another task body mentions | File pointer: grep draft task bodies for the new path and add `depends_on` |
| Has an unsettled interface | Stop decomposing; in plan mode return to the plan growth loop, otherwise hand off to `varde-change plan` |

Investigate codebase unknowns directly; `kind: research` is only for lasting
external output. Add a doc task (writing `<knowledge>/reference/` or
`<knowledge>/flows/`, depending on all implementation tasks) only when asked.

## 2. Build the breakdown

Require per task (no step count or named test function):

- an observable outcome;
- expected files touched, if known; otherwise say so and let the builder find
  them;
- dependencies and risks;
- the `assert:`/`retrieve:` checks proving the slice works;
- `#### Test approach`: one profile (`tdd`, `regression`,
  `characterization`, `smoke`, or `not-applicable`) and a one-line rationale.

Profile authority, highest first:

1. Direct user instructions.
2. Repository policy.
3. The default: test-first for behavior changes.

Name the directive in the rationale when one set the profile; any other
choice (characterization for fragile legacy code, smoke for packaging) states
its reason there.

## 3. Declare ownership

- Trace each changed behavior to its consuming tests and required helpers;
  include their writes in ownership, including tests of interim behavior.
- Limit pinned-text checks to tracked files that consume or assert the task
  output. Matching text alone does not establish a dependency.
- Declare every written path in `modifies`, `creates`, and `renames` (each
  rename as `old/path -> new/path`).
- Name every shared database, snapshot, or other external state the task or
  its checks use or change in `verification_resources`.
- The plan lists generated outputs and their generator commands; no task owns
  them.
- Use `[]` for an empty category; omit a field whose contents are unknown so
  automatic scheduling stays serial.
- A behavior-preserving restructuring task sets `posture: refactor` so
  `varde work execution-wave` isolates it in a worktree.

## 4. Check each task's size

A task is the smallest execution-safe unit. Rewrite and re-check any task that
fails one of these:

- Exactly one public behavior or workflow rule changes, with one observable
  outcome and no open choices.
- It fits one builder; split on evidence (a run that blocked or hit its
  context limit), not on an estimate.
- A schema/persistence change names the file where the schema lives, found by
  reading, not analogy.

## 5. Present and record

Check new or rewritten verification commands against the baseline before
finalizing; record expected failures and generated writes in the task.

1. Interactive: show the breakdown as a table and pause once for missing,
   wrong-scoped, or badly split tasks. Unattended runs skip the pause.
2. Write each task from `assets/TASK-TEMPLATE.md` in the plan's `tasks/`
   directory, with populated `modifies`, `creates`, `depends_on`, and
   `status: todo`. Task IDs are kebab-case with no date prefix, unique across
   every plan's `tasks/*.md`. Readiness is computed live from `depends_on`,
   never stored.
=== skills/varde-change/references/plan.md ===
# Plan

## Resume a draft

When asked to resume planning with no feature named:

- **Find drafts.** A draft is a `plan.md` with `status: backlog` and an id
  ending in `-draft` or `-draft-<n>`, or a live Open Questions bullet. Search
  at any depth under `<working>/plans/`. Nested child plans count; their id is
  their path, such as `<group-id>/<child-id>`.
- **Ask.** List every draft as a numbered `title - plan id` list and ask which
  to resume, then continue with [The growth loop](#the-growth-loop). If there
  are none, wait for the user's idea and [start a plan](#start-a-plan).

## Start a plan

### First turn

Include `varde map context_pack` with feature terms when available. In the
same read-only discovery call, scan `<working>/reviews/deferred/`.

1. Pick a temporary slug from the prompt and run
   `scripts/plan-path.py draft --working <working> --slug <slug>`; it creates
   and prints the draft directory, whose name is the plan id until
   finalization. Create `plan.md` there from `assets/PLAN-TEMPLATE.md` with
   Write/Edit, and set `title` to the initial prompt.
2. Seed genuine best guesses immediately in the template's formats, including
   Given/When/Then criteria and every unknown as an Open Question or Assumption.
   List deferred findings with a blank `Disposition` and an in-scope `Location`
   as Open Questions with their review date, deduplicating copies by `Source`
   and original id. The user decides to include or defer; never add one
   automatically.
3. Tell the user the plan path and welcome direct edits. Ask the one highest-value question per
   [Asking questions](#asking-questions), then wait.

## The growth loop

Each turn, research what the repo can answer. Load
`references/varde-code-cli.md` only when `varde` is on PATH and scope or
dependents are unknown.

### Routing unknowns

Route every unknown instead of blocking; impact beats confidence:

- **Code or search can answer it:** research it; don't list it.
- **Confident, and a wrong guess stays inside one Design subsection:**
  `## Assumptions` with `confidence: high`; don't spend a turn.
- **Needs something concrete** (an open UI shape, interaction feel, a state
  model, or a layout tradeoff visible only once built): mark it
  `[needs prototype]`, invoke `varde-prototype`, and resume with its answer.
  Skip this when the UI shape is already settled.
- **Everything else** (unsure, or touching the plan split, AC, an external
  contract, or solution shape): `## Open Questions` with a recommendation, and
  ask.

**Push back.** Challenge the idea and propose a better, smaller shape when
you see one:

- If the scenario is speculative or an existing capability seems to cover it,
  offer do-not-build ("This looks like [X] already covers it. Build anyway, or
  is this a non-issue?").
- Close as do-not-build only on explicit agreement, then discard the plan
  directory.

### Terminology and standards

Once the seed makes the domain concrete, search `<knowledge>/` for the
feature's specs, decisions, definitions, and patterns:

- Link the ones that apply under `## Related`.
- Put any that look stale into `## Open Questions` as one item.
- Record a missing definition with `varde-knowledge`.
- When `<knowledge>/specs/<domain>.md` covers code this plan changes, add the
  domain to `observed_specs` and pass its spec file at Finalize step 3's
  `review init` (`--scope`, or `--artifact <absolute-file>` outside the
  repository); after init, add it with `review expand` and a fresh pre-edit
  verdict.

### Per-turn steps

1. **Watch the doc.** Re-read `plan.md` and diff it against your last
   snapshot. A change you did not make to `## Open Questions`,
   `## Assumptions`, `## Design`, `## Non-goals`, or `## Constraints` is a
   user edit that counts as an answer; process it with the chat message.
2. **Resolve items.** Write each decision into its `## Design` subsection (or
   Non-goals/Constraints) in the template's form, append
   `<question> → <answer>` to `## Decisions so far`, remove the resolved
   line, and add any unknowns the answer exposes. An accepted assumption moves
   to the decision log too.
3. **Ask** the highest-value Open Question per [Asking questions](#asking-questions),
   solution-shape questions before spelling ones.

Throughout:

- **Single writer.** Only this session edits `plan.md`. Research subagents get
  the resolved absolute `<working>` and `<knowledge>` paths, use them without
  re-resolving storage, and return findings.

### Exit criteria

Each turn, route implicit assumptions in Design/AC per
[Routing unknowns](#routing-unknowns). Run [Self-review](#self-review) when
`## Open Questions` first has no live item, and again at Finalize. Finalize
when `## Open Questions` has no live item and the final self-review finds
nothing new.

## External interface check

If a touched surface has existing consumers (exported API, CLI flag, env var,
CI config, shared type, or a file others read), flag it explicitly and find
them with `dependents`/`blast_radius` from `varde map` and
`references/varde-code-cli.md`, or grep otherwise. Record them in Design and
AC.

## Self-review

When run, an empty `## Open Questions` is not done. Add an Open Question for
each of these and continue:

- placeholders (TBD, vague Design);
- contradictions between decisions;
- scope the Solution implies but Non-goals omits;
- decisions admitting two implementations.

When scope outside fenced code blocks adds a second case to a formerly
single-case model, makes a required field optional, or turns a derived or
fixed value into a choice, and `## Decisions so far` does not already resolve
that shift, add one Open Question: promote the general model, or add it
alongside the old one?

## Acceptance criteria

Criteria are plan-level: true after ship, however build slices it. Review the
full set before the final completeness check:

- **`assert:`** (preferred): a command, grep, or test whose pass/fail needs no
  LLM judgment.
- **`retrieve:`**: the file(s) or grep an LLM must read and judge, and what it
  looks for. An agent grading text it just produced is biased, so first try to
  restate it as `assert:` (command, exit code, file existence, non-empty
  output). Keep it only for semantic judgment no command can give, such as
  whether an error message explains the cause.
- **Testable as written:** each criterion names a command or a file a reader
  judges.

## Finalize

1. **Rename and validate.**
   - Derive the slug from the plan's title or problem (lowercase, hyphenated)
     without asking, and run
     `scripts/plan-path.py finalize --draft <plan-dir> --slug <slug>`. It
     renames the directory, keeping the draft's date, and prints the new path
     and `ignored: true|false`; record `ignored`.
   - Run `varde work validate <plan-dir>/plan.md --json` and fix
     diagnostics before review.
2. **Split or decompose before review.** For several independently shippable
   changes, [split](#split-into-child-plans) first: the parent gets no tasks. Otherwise follow `references/plan-decomposition.md`.
3. **Establish review location and review.** Establish the visible plan
   worktree per `references/build-worktree.md` without committing before step
   5's approval (unless a specific checkpoint is already authorized); map tracked
   plan files there, retain external storage, and initialize the exact-root subject
   (`review init --plan <plan.md>`, with `observed_specs` files) per
   `references/review-gate-plan.md` §1 and `references/review-gates.md`.
   Give an independent reviewer the plan/tasks, subject/scope, and resolved
   `<working>`/`<knowledge>` paths to check splits, execution-wave independence,
   context estimates, assumptions, human choices, criteria, and shippability.
   It inspects `pre-edit` and writes its own `varde work review record`; keep
   the subject id in plan Progress for build/resume.
4. **Apply the review.** Apply findings and review every criterion per
   [Acceptance criteria](#acceptance-criteria), investigating code-answerable
   unknowns and returning human decisions to the interview. For several
   changes, follow [Split into child plans](#split-into-child-plans) instead of
   step 5. Revalidate after edits; a materially changed plan needs fresh
   inspection and independent approval, otherwise the approved verdict carries
   to build.
5. Ask the **final completeness check**: unseen assumptions and changes from
   steps 2-4, one line each, grouped by impact. Link the plan and approval
   worktree, branch/base; explicitly request local plan/task commit
   authorization while reserving target integration for separate approval.
   Ask "Anything left to resolve before we finalize?" Wait for confirmation;
   apply requested changes, revalidate/review, and repeat when needed.

6. After confirmation, no more questions or content changes. The plan stays
   `backlog` until build moves it to `active`.
7. Reuse step 1's reported `ignored` value: ignored plans stay local;
   otherwise commit only the plan directory on its authorized plan branch,
   never the user's target branch.
8. Announce that `Plan <plan-id> is ready; ask to build it.`

### Split into child plans

Use this at Finalize step 2, or step 4 when review finds several shippable
changes; from step 4, first delete the parent's task files and note in
Progress that its subject is abandoned.

1. List candidate titles and dependency order. Ask whether any should be
   combined or split differently, then wait.
2. Establish one visible group plan worktree per
   `references/build-worktree.md` as the exact approval root for parent and
   children, before their finalization reviews. Create nested child plans at
   `<working>/plans/<plan-id>/<child-slug>/plan.md`. The path gives each child
   its compound id and group membership, so no `children:`/`parent:` fields
   are needed. Finalize each child with Finalize step 1's validate only
   (never `plan-path.py finalize`), then steps 2-8; build decomposes each
   later.
3. Keep the current plan as the group parent with `shape: group` in
   frontmatter. Keep its goal, non-goals, constraints, and aggregate contract
   outside Progress: source scope, child ids/dependencies/contracts,
   assumptions, and aggregate acceptance/verification. Validate it, then
   initialize its subject over the aggregate source scope (Finalize step 3's
   `review init --plan`, with the owning approval repoRoot). Get independent
   `pre-edit` approval of the combined contract in the same reviewer session
   as the children's step 3 reviews, one record per subject; keep the subject
   id in the parent's Progress. Commit the parent with its children only on
   the authorized group plan branch when storage is tracked, then finish the
   parent with Finalize steps 7-8 only.

## Asking questions

Up to three questions may share a turn when they are facets of one decision
or share candidate solutions, such as naming sibling commands or edge cases of
one input. Silence and surrounding context leave the decision open. Use this
menu:

```
<Question>

  1. <Option A>
  2. <Option B>
  3. Other - describe what you want

Recommendation: <n> (<label>) - <one-sentence reason>.
```
=== skills/varde-change/references/status.md ===
# Change status

Read-only: change no plan, task, or handoff. Show:

- **Plans:** every `plan.md` at any depth under `<working>/plans/` not
  `completed`; date-prefixed ids newest first, others last; top 5 plus
  remaining count. Columns Status | Plan | Tasks | Done (from `tasks/*.md`
  frontmatter only); a group's children list under it. Empty:
  `No plans in a non-terminal status.`
- **Handoffs:** `<working>/handoffs/*/handoff.md` with `status: open`, newest
  5 plus remaining count (Handoff | Description | Timestamp | Linked plan
  status). Empty: `No open handoffs.`
- **Next mode:** use `varde work readiness <plan.md> --json`
  blockers/actions when available. Recommend one mode as
  `Recommended next mode: <mode>`, then stop; never run it:
  - `plan`: unplanned work, or resume a draft per
    `references/plan.md` (Resume a draft);
  - `build`: one ready plan;
  - `orchestrate`: ready group children;
  - `verify`: aggregate evidence.
=== skills/varde-change/references/verify.md ===
# Standalone verification

Read-only: never fix, change status, or tick criteria.

## Resolve the target

| Request | Target |
|---|---|
| Plan identifier or slug | Matching `<working>/plans/<plan-id>/plan.md` |
| Feature or group | Group plan and every nested child plan |
| No target | Most recent completed date-prefixed plan; none: report that and stop |

List ambiguous slug matches and ask once.
State the resolved identifier and current status.

## Verify

1. Read `## Acceptance criteria`. Stop if missing, except for a group parent
   without it: verify each child plan, then report the aggregate.
2. Ignore checkbox state; a check is a claim, not evidence, and an unchecked
   one is not an automatic failure.
3. Read each adjacent `tasks/*.md` status and Progress evidence.
   Do not re-grade task Verification blocks.
4. Run every criterion's `assert:` command or structural check, exactly as
   written — never silently substitute a different assertion, and run broad
   project checks only when a criterion asks for one.
   Compare its exact expected result.
   Record exit codes or match counts.
5. For every `retrieve:` clause, read only named files.
   Compare the requested outcome and record its supporting line.
6. Classify every criterion:
   - `passed`: evidence matches expectations.
   - `failed`: evidence exists but contradicts expectations.
   - `unavailable`: evidence cannot be gathered — including a missing command
     or a moved file.
7. Report each criterion with its evidence.
   Finish with outcome counts and plan status.

A UI check needs a browser tool from your own tool list; harness tools do not
appear on `PATH`. Without one, the check is `unavailable`, never passed; never
infer rendering from an HTTP fetch or source. Log in only with
credentials the user supplied, and submit no form that changes real data.

Recommend `varde-change build` when fixes are needed.
=== skills/varde-change/references/workflow-state.md ===
# Workflow state

An unknown status (`draft`, or a task in `backlog`) makes later CLI calls fail
with `unknown status`.

| Artifact | States | Initial | Legal moves |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plan` | `backlog`, `active`, `blocked`, `completed` | `backlog` | `backlog` to `active` or `blocked`; `active` to `blocked` or `completed`; `blocked` to `active`; `completed` is terminal |
| `task` | `todo`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `done` | `todo` | `todo` to `in_progress` or `blocked`; `in_progress` to `blocked` or `done`; `blocked` to `in_progress`; `done` is terminal |

Change status through `transition`, never by editing `status` directly:

```bash
varde work readiness <plan.md> --json
varde work transition <artifact.md> <state> --json
varde work validate <artifact.md> --json
```

- A rejected transition (`workflow_blocked`) lists legal states and changes no
  bytes.
- `recover --root <project-root>` finishes an interrupted accepted transition.
=== skills/varde-change/scripts/plan-path.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Allocate and finalize plan directory paths.

  plan-path.py draft --working <dir> --slug <slug>
  plan-path.py finalize --draft <plan-dir> --slug <slug>

draft creates <working>/plans/<UTC-date>-<slug>-draft[-N]/ and prints it.
finalize renames a draft to <draft-date>-<slug> and prints the new path and
`ignored: true|false`. Ignored plans and plans outside a repo use a plain
move; tracked drafts use `git mv`. An existing destination is refused.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def git(cwd, *args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(cwd), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)


def draft(working, slug):
    plans = Path(working) / "plans"
    base = f"{datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc):%Y-%m-%d}-{slug}-draft"
    target, n = plans / base, 1
    while target.exists():
        n += 1
        target = plans / f"{base}-{n}"
    target.mkdir(parents=True)
    print(target)


def finalize(draft_dir, slug):
    src = Path(draft_dir).absolute()
    date = re.match(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", src.name)
    if not date:
        sys.exit(f"draft name has no leading date: {src.name}")
    dest = src.parent / f"{date.group()}-{slug}"
    if dest.exists():
        sys.exit(f"destination exists: {dest}")
    in_repo = git(src, "rev-parse", "--is-inside-work-tree").returncode == 0
    ignored = not in_repo or git(src, "check-ignore", "-q", str(dest / "plan.md")).returncode == 0
    tracked = in_repo and not ignored and bool(git(src, "ls-files", str(src)).stdout.strip())
    if tracked:
        moved = git(src.parent, "mv", str(src), str(dest))
        if moved.returncode:
            sys.exit(moved.stderr.strip())
    else:
        shutil.move(str(src), str(dest))
    print(dest)
    print(f"ignored: {str(ignored).lower()}")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    d = sub.add_parser("draft")
    d.add_argument("--working", required=True)
    d.add_argument("--slug", required=True)
    f = sub.add_parser("finalize")
    f.add_argument("--draft", required=True)
    f.add_argument("--slug", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "draft":
        draft(args.working, args.slug)
    else:
        finalize(args.draft, args.slug)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
=== skills/varde-change/scripts/select-plans.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.9"
# dependencies = []
# ///
"""List the plans `varde-change` build can select.

Usage: select-plans.py --working DIR

Reads every `plan.md` at any depth under DIR/plans. Skips `shape: group` plans
and drafts (id ending `-draft` or `-draft-<digits>`, or a live bullet under `## Open Questions`).
Keeps `backlog` and `active` plans. With `varde` on PATH it runs
`varde work readiness <plan> --json` per plan and
`varde work graph <plan> --json --all` per candidate. The graph covers one
plan's `depends_on` closure, so every candidate is checked. The script excludes
plans with an incomplete dependency or named by a `dependency_cycle` blocker,
then puts backlog plans first and sorts each status group by id.

Output (stdout, exit 0):
  {plans: [{id, title, status, implementation_ready, blockers: [...]}],
   excluded_by_dependency: N, cycles: [ids], degraded: bool,
   degraded_plans: [ids]}

`degraded` is true when `varde` is missing or a call failed;
`degraded_plans` lists the affected ids. Those plans are filtered by their
`depends_on` front matter instead: any dependency not `completed` excludes
the plan. Failure prints {"error", "message"} and
exits 1 (usage or unreadable working directory).
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def fail(name, message):
    print(json.dumps({"error": name, "message": message}))
    sys.exit(1)


def parse_list(value, following):
    """Parse an inline `[a, b]` or block `- a` YAML list of ids."""
    value = value.strip()
    if value.startswith("["):
        items = value.strip("[]").split(",")
    else:
        items = []
        for line in following:
            if not re.match(r"\s*-\s", line) and line.strip():
                break
            if line.strip():
                items.append(line.strip()[1:])
    return [i.strip().strip("\"'") for i in items if i.strip().strip("\"'")]


def read_plan(path):
    """Return (id, title, status, shape, has_open_question, depends_on) or None."""
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    match = re.match(r"---\n(.*?)\n---", text, re.S)
    if not match:
        return None
    front = {}
    depends = []
    lines = match.group(1).splitlines()
    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
        key, sep, value = line.partition(":")
        if sep and not line.startswith((" ", "-")):
            front[key.strip()] = value.strip().strip("\"'")
            if key.strip() == "depends_on":
                depends = parse_list(value, lines[number + 1:])
    body = text[match.end():]
    live = False
    section = re.search(r"^## Open Questions\s*\n(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)", body, re.S | re.M)
    if section:
        live = bool(re.search(r"^\s*[-*] ", section.group(1), re.M))
    return (front.get("id") or path.parent.name, front.get("title", ""),
            front.get("status", ""), front.get("shape", ""), live, depends)


def dependency_status(path, statuses):
    """Status of a dependency plan.md, reading it when outside the scanned plans."""
    path = path.resolve()
    if path not in statuses:
        try:
            info = read_plan(path) if path.is_file() else None
        except OSError:
            info = None
        statuses[path] = info[2] if info else None
    return statuses[path]


def workflow(args):
    """Return the `data` object from a varde work command, or None."""
    try:
        done = subprocess.run(["varde", "work", *args, "--json"], capture_output=True,
                              text=True, timeout=60)
        if done.returncode != 0:
            return None
        return json.loads(done.stdout)["data"]
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--working", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    plans_dir = Path(args.working) / "plans"
    if not plans_dir.is_dir():
        fail("working_missing", f"no plans directory at {plans_dir}")

    candidates = []
    statuses = {}
    for path in sorted(plans_dir.rglob("plan.md")):
        info = read_plan(path)
        if not info:
            continue
        plan_id, title, status, shape, live, depends = info
        statuses[path.resolve()] = status
        if shape == "group" or re.search(r"-draft(-\d+)?$", plan_id) or live:
            continue
        if status in ("backlog", "active"):
            candidates.append({"id": plan_id, "title": title, "status": status,
                               "path": path, "depends": depends})

    have_cli = shutil.which("varde") is not None
    degraded_plans = set() if have_cli else {c["id"] for c in candidates}
    cycles = []
    excluded = 0
    plans = []
    if have_cli:
        for plan in candidates:
            graph = workflow(["graph", str(plan["path"]), "--all"])
            if graph is None:
                degraded_plans.add(plan["id"])
                continue
            for blocker in graph["blockers"]:
                if blocker.get("code") == "dependency_cycle":
                    for name in (blocker.get("artifact_id"), blocker.get("dependency")):
                        if name and name not in cycles:
                            cycles.append(name)
    for plan in candidates:
        ready, blockers = False, []
        data = None
        if plan["id"] not in degraded_plans:
            data = workflow(["readiness", str(plan["path"])])
            if data is None:
                degraded_plans.add(plan["id"])
        if data is None:
            # Resolve like varde work: <plan_dir>/../<dep>/plan.md, no id fallback.
            plan_dir = plan["path"].parent
            if any(dependency_status(plan_dir.parent / d / "plan.md", statuses) != "completed"
                   for d in plan["depends"]):
                excluded += 1
                continue
        else:
            blockers = list(data["blockers"])
            blockers += (data.get("review") or {}).get("blockers", [])
            ready = bool(data["implementation_ready"])
            if not data["planning_ready"] or plan["id"] in cycles:
                excluded += 1
                continue
        plans.append({"id": plan["id"], "title": plan["title"], "status": plan["status"],
                      "implementation_ready": ready, "blockers": blockers})
    plans.sort(key=lambda p: (p["status"] != "backlog", p["id"]))
    print(json.dumps({"plans": plans, "excluded_by_dependency": excluded,
                      "cycles": sorted(cycles), "degraded": bool(degraded_plans),
                      "degraded_plans": sorted(degraded_plans)}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
=== skills/varde-change/scripts/worktree-cleanup.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remove a registered worktree and its branch after merge or explicit discard.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: worktree-cleanup.sh [--discard] <id>

Removes the registered worktree on branch worktree/<id> and deletes that
branch. Normal cleanup requires a worktree with no uncommitted or ignored
files whose branch is merged into the currently checked-out commit. Use
--discard only when deliberately abandoning its committed or local work.

Exit codes:
  0  worktree and branch removed
  1  usage error or cleanup could not be completed safely
EOF
}

fail() {
  echo "error: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  usage
  exit 0
fi

discard=false
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--discard" ]]; then
  discard=true
  shift
fi

if [[ $# -ne 1 || "$1" == -* ]]; then
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

id="$1"
branch="worktree/${id}"
branch_ref="refs/heads/${branch}"
git check-ref-format "$branch_ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "invalid worktree id '${id}'"

git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
  fail "not inside a Git worktree"
git show-ref --verify --quiet "$branch_ref" || fail "branch ${branch} does not exist"
branch_oid="$(git rev-parse --verify "$branch_ref")" || fail "could not resolve branch ${branch}"

# Resolve by the branch recorded by Git, not by a path inferred from the
# current checkout. The caller may be in the main checkout or any linked tree.
registry="$(git worktree list --porcelain)" || fail "could not list registered worktrees"
target_path=""
record_path=""
record_branch=""
matches=0

record_target_if_matching() {
  if [[ -n "$record_path" && "$record_branch" == "$branch_ref" ]]; then
    matches=$((matches + 1))
    target_path="$record_path"
  fi
}

while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
  case "$line" in
    "worktree "*)
      record_target_if_matching
      record_path="${line#worktree }"
      record_branch=""
      ;;
    "branch "*)
      record_branch="${line#branch }"
      ;;
    "")
      record_target_if_matching
      record_path=""
      record_branch=""
      ;;
  esac
done <<< "$registry"
record_target_if_matching

[[ "$matches" -eq 1 ]] || {
  if [[ "$matches" -eq 0 ]]; then
    fail "no registered worktree uses branch ${branch}"
  fi
  fail "multiple registered worktrees use branch ${branch}; refusing cleanup"
}

[[ -d "$target_path" ]] || fail "registered worktree path is unavailable: ${target_path}"
target_realpath="$(cd "$target_path" && pwd -P)" ||
  fail "registered worktree path is unavailable: ${target_path}"
caller_realpath="$(pwd -P)"
case "$caller_realpath/" in
  "$target_realpath/"*) fail "cannot clean up the worktree that contains the current directory" ;;
esac

if [[ "$discard" != true ]]; then
  worktree_status="$(git -C "$target_path" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all 2>/dev/null)" ||
    fail "registered worktree is unavailable: ${target_path}"
  [[ -z "$worktree_status" ]] || fail "worktree ${id} has uncommitted changes; use --discard only to abandon them"

  ignored_status="$(git -C "$target_path" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored 2>/dev/null)" ||
    fail "could not inspect ignored files in worktree ${id}"
  [[ -z "$ignored_status" ]] || fail "worktree ${id} has ignored files; use --discard only to abandon them"

  if git merge-base --is-ancestor "$branch_oid" HEAD; then
    :
  else
    merge_status=$?
    if [[ "$merge_status" -eq 1 ]]; then
      fail "branch ${branch} is not merged into the currently checked-out commit; use --discard only to abandon it"
    fi
    fail "could not verify whether branch ${branch} is merged"
  fi
fi

if [[ "$discard" == true ]]; then
  git worktree remove --force "$target_path" || fail "could not discard worktree ${target_path}"
else
  git worktree remove "$target_path" || fail "could not remove clean worktree ${target_path}"
fi

remaining_registry="$(git worktree list --porcelain)" || fail "could not verify worktree removal"
while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
  if [[ "$line" == "worktree ${target_path}" ]]; then
    fail "worktree ${target_path} remains registered after removal"
  fi
done <<< "$remaining_registry"

git update-ref -d "$branch_ref" "$branch_oid" ||
  fail "worktree was removed, but branch ${branch} changed after preflight or could not be deleted safely"

if git show-ref --verify --quiet "$branch_ref"; then
  fail "branch ${branch} remains after removal"
else
  show_ref_status=$?
  [[ "$show_ref_status" -eq 1 ]] || fail "could not verify branch removal for ${branch}"
fi

if [[ "$discard" == true ]]; then
  echo "discarded worktree and branch for ${id}"
else
  echo "removed worktree and branch for ${id}"
fi
=== skills/varde-change/scripts/worktree-create.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Create an isolated git worktree pinned to a fixed base SHA.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: worktree-create.sh [--fresh] <id> [base]
       worktree-create.sh --plan <id> <explicit-base>

Creates a worktree for <id> at <repo>/.varde/worktrees/<id>, branched from
<base> (default: HEAD), pinned to that commit's resolved SHA. New worktrees
require a clean, committed caller. --fresh allocates a sibling even inside
a linked worktree; without it, a linked caller keeps ownership and is reused.
--plan always creates a fresh plan worktree at an explicit committed base;
it permits a dirty origin and leaves its branch, index and local files intact.

Prints three lines on success:
  path=<worktree-path>
  branch=<branch>
  created=<true|false>

created=true  a fresh worktree was made and the caller OWNS it — the caller
              must merge + cleanup when done.
created=false the caller is already inside a linked worktree, so this is a
              no-op that reuses it; the caller must NOT merge or cleanup
              (whoever created the outer worktree owns that).

Exit codes:
  0  worktree created, or reused because already inside a linked worktree
  1  usage error
  2  <base> did not resolve to a commit
  3  a worktree or branch for <id> already exists
  4  caller is dirty, detached, or has no committed HEAD
EOF
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  usage
  exit 0
fi

fresh=false
plan=false
case "${1:-}" in
  --fresh) fresh=true; shift ;;
  --plan) fresh=true; plan=true; shift ;;
esac
if [[ $# -lt 1 || $# -gt 2 || "${1:-}" == -* || "${2:-}" == --plan || "${2:-}" == --fresh ]] ||
   { [[ "$plan" == true ]] && [[ $# -ne 2 || -z "${2:-}" ]]; }; then
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

id="$1"
base="${2:-HEAD}"

base_sha="$(git rev-parse --verify "${base}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null)" || {
  echo "error: base '${base}' did not resolve to a commit" >&2
  exit 2
}

# Already inside a linked worktree? Then the caller is already isolated —
# reuse it instead of nesting a second worktree. --git-dir and --git-common-dir
# diverge only inside a linked worktree; they're identical in the main checkout.
if [[ "$fresh" == false && "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" != "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" ]]; then
  echo "note: already inside a linked worktree — reusing it, no new worktree created" >&2
  echo "path=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  echo "branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
  echo "created=false"
  exit 0
fi

repo_root="$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)")"
worktree_path="${repo_root}/.varde/worktrees/${id}"
branch="worktree/${id}"

if git worktree list --porcelain | grep -x "worktree ${worktree_path}" >/dev/null; then
  echo "error: worktree already exists at ${worktree_path}" >&2
  exit 3
fi
if git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/${branch}"; then
  echo "error: branch ${branch} already exists" >&2
  exit 3
fi

git check-ref-format "refs/heads/$branch" >/dev/null || { echo "error: invalid worktree id '${id}'" >&2; exit 1; }
if [[ "$plan" == false ]] && {
   [[ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]] ||
   ! git symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD >/dev/null ||
   ! git rev-parse --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1;
}; then
  echo "error: caller must be clean and on a committed branch" >&2
  exit 4
fi
mkdir -p "$(dirname "${worktree_path}")"
# Keep the nested worktrees out of the main checkout's status without editing
# any tracked .gitignore.
exclude="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)/info/exclude"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "${exclude}")"
grep -qx '/.varde/' "${exclude}" 2>/dev/null || echo '/.varde/' >> "${exclude}"
git worktree add -b "${branch}" "${worktree_path}" "${base_sha}" >&2

echo "path=${worktree_path}"
echo "branch=${branch}"
echo "created=true"
=== skills/varde-change/scripts/worktree-merge.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Merge a worktree's branch back into the target branch.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: worktree-merge.sh <id> [into]

Merges worktree/<id> into <into> (default: the branch currently checked out
in this checkout). An explicit <into> must name that checked-out branch. Does
NOT commit on the caller's behalf — the worktree must be clean.

Exit codes:
  0  merged cleanly, worktree/<id> is now in <into>
  1  usage error
  2  worktree/<id> has no commits ahead of its base — nothing to merge
  3  merge conflict — resolve via references/build-worktree.md, then finish the
     merge manually; do NOT run worktree-cleanup.sh until it's resolved
  4  target rejected: branch/<id> is missing, <into> does not resolve, <into>
     does not name the currently checked-out branch, or the merge failed for
     a reason other than conflict
  5  worktree/<id> has uncommitted changes — the task did not complete;
     caller decides
EOF
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  usage
  exit 0
fi

if [[ $# -lt 1 || $# -gt 2 ]]; then
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

id="$1"
branch="worktree/${id}"
into="${2:-$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)}"
current_ref="$(git symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"

if [[ $# -eq 2 ]]; then
  target_ref="$(git rev-parse --symbolic-full-name "${into}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [[ -z "${current_ref}" || ( "${into}" != "HEAD" && "${target_ref}" != "${current_ref}" ) ]]; then
    echo "error: target ${into} is not the currently checked-out branch" >&2
    exit 4
  fi
fi

common_git_dir="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"
repo_root="$(dirname "${common_git_dir}")"
worktree_path="${repo_root}/.varde/worktrees/${id}"

git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${branch}^{commit}" >/dev/null || { echo "error: branch ${branch} does not exist" >&2; exit 4; }
git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${into}^{commit}" >/dev/null || { echo "error: target ${into} does not resolve" >&2; exit 4; }
if [[ -d "${worktree_path}" ]] && [[ -n "$(git -C "${worktree_path}" status --porcelain)" ]]; then
  echo "error: worktree/${id} has uncommitted changes — the task did not complete" >&2
  exit 5
fi

merge_base="$(git merge-base "${into}" "${branch}")"
if [[ "$(git rev-parse "${branch}")" == "${merge_base}" ]]; then
  echo "error: ${branch} has no commits ahead of ${into} — nothing to merge" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if git merge --no-ff --no-edit "${branch}"; then
  echo "merged ${branch} into ${into}"
  exit 0
else
  if ! git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | grep . >/dev/null; then
    echo "error: merge failed without conflicts" >&2
    exit 4
  fi
  echo "conflict merging ${branch} into ${into} — see references/build-worktree.md" >&2
  exit 3
fi
=== skills/varde-change/scripts/worktree-permissions.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Describe and probe a bound worker's session permissions, without global config."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import uuid


def run(argv, cwd=None, env=None):
    return subprocess.check_output(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, text=True).strip()


def git(root, *args, env=None):
    return run(['git', '-C', str(root), *args], env=env)


def git_path(root, *args):
    return str((Path(root) / git(root, 'rev-parse', *args)).resolve())


def describe(repository, worktree, subject, binding, extra):
    repository = Path(repository).resolve(strict=True)
    worktree = Path(worktree).resolve(strict=True)
    for root in (repository, worktree):
        if Path(git(root, 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel')).resolve() != root:
            raise RuntimeError(f'not an exact checkout root: {root}')
    common = git_path(worktree, '--git-common-dir')
    if git_path(repository, '--git-common-dir') != common:
        raise RuntimeError('approval and worker belong to different Git repositories')
    admin = git_path(worktree, '--absolute-git-dir')
    approval_admin = git_path(repository, '--absolute-git-dir')
    index = git_path(worktree, '--git-path', 'index')
    objects = git_path(worktree, '--git-path', 'objects')
    extras = [str(Path(p).resolve(strict=True)) for p in extra]
    # ProjectLock::acquire uses root/.varde-workflow.lock for ordinary
    # checkouts and acquire_worktree uses the linked Git admin instead.
    approval_lock = str((Path(approval_admin) if (repository / '.git').is_file()
                         else repository) / '.varde-workflow.lock')
    writes = list(dict.fromkeys([str(worktree), approval_admin, admin, common,
                                 objects, str(Path(index).parent), *extras]))
    directory_probes = writes.copy()
    writes = list(dict.fromkeys([*writes, approval_lock]))
    return dict(approval_lock=approval_lock,
                worker_lock=str(Path(admin) / '.varde-workflow.lock'),
                directory_probes=directory_probes,
                permission_reasons={'approval_lock': 'bound review lock',
                                    'directory_probes': 'worker and structural Git/verification writes'},
                repository=str(repository), worktree=str(worktree), subject=subject,
                binding=binding, approval_git_admin=approval_admin,
                worker_git_admin=admin, common_git=common, index=index,
                objects=objects, writes=writes,
                approval_evidence={'path': str(repository), 'access': 'read'},
                working_store='read-only unless explicitly supplied with --write',
                extra_verification_dirs=extras)


def probe_directory(directory):
    name = None
    renamed = None
    try:
        fd, name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='varde-probe-', dir=directory)
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'wb') as stream:
            stream.write(b'permission probe\n')
        rename_fd, renamed = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='varde-probe-', dir=directory)
        os.close(rename_fd)
        os.rename(name, renamed)
        name = None
    finally:
        for filename in (name, renamed):
            if filename and os.path.lexists(filename):
                os.unlink(filename)


def review_gate(manifest):
    output = run(['varde', 'work', 'review', 'check', '--repository', manifest['repository'],
         '--worktree', manifest['worktree'], '--subject', manifest['subject'],
         '--binding', manifest['binding'], '--checkpoint', 'start', '--json'],
        cwd=manifest['worktree'], env=dict(os.environ, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS='0'))
    result = json.loads(output)
    if result.get('ok') is not True or result.get('data', {}).get('ready') is not True:
        raise RuntimeError('bound start review check did not report ok and ready')


def check(manifest, gate=review_gate):
    worker = manifest['worktree']
    if Path.cwd().resolve() != Path(worker):
        raise RuntimeError('check must run in the exact physical worker cwd')
    index = Path(manifest['index'])
    original_index = index.read_bytes() if index.exists() else None
    original_head = git(worker, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD')
    original_branch = git(worker, 'rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD')
    original_status = git(worker, '--no-optional-locks', 'status', '--porcelain=v1', '--untracked-files=all')
    gate(manifest)  # Real binding check before any write, never escalated here.
    for directory in manifest['directory_probes']:
        probe_directory(directory)
    fd, temporary_index = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='varde-probe-', dir=index.parent)
    os.close(fd)
    os.unlink(temporary_index)
    env = dict(os.environ, GIT_INDEX_FILE=temporary_index,
               GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Varde permission probe',
               GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='probe@example.invalid',
               GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Varde permission probe',
               GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='probe@example.invalid')
    ref = 'refs/varde-permission-probes/' + uuid.uuid4().hex
    commit = None
    ref_created = False
    try:
        git(worker, 'read-tree', 'HEAD', env=env)
        tree = git(worker, 'write-tree', env=env)
        commit = git(worker, '-c', 'commit.gpgsign=false', 'commit-tree', tree,
                     '-p', original_head, '-m', 'Disposable permission probe ' + ref, env=env)
        git(worker, 'update-ref', '--create-reflog', ref, commit, '')
        ref_created = True
        git(worker, 'update-ref', '-d', ref, commit)
        ref_created = False
    finally:
        if commit:
            print('probe commit retained for normal Git pruning after ref cleanup: ' + commit,
                  file=sys.stderr)
        # Attempt every cleanup even when one fails; never remove foreign files.
        cleanup_errors = []
        if ref_created:
            try:
                git(worker, 'update-ref', '-d', ref, commit)
            except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
                cleanup_errors.append(f'{ref}: {error}')
        for candidate in (temporary_index, temporary_index + '.lock'):
            try:
                if os.path.lexists(candidate):
                    os.unlink(candidate)
            except OSError as error:
                cleanup_errors.append(f'{candidate}: {error}')
        if cleanup_errors:
            raise RuntimeError('probe cleanup failed: ' + '; '.join(cleanup_errors))
    if ((index.read_bytes() if index.exists() else None) != original_index
            or git(worker, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD') != original_head
            or git(worker, 'rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD') != original_branch
            or git(worker, '--no-optional-locks', 'status', '--porcelain=v1', '--untracked-files=all') != original_status):
        raise RuntimeError('probe detected changed HEAD, branch, real index, or worktree status')
    return dict(passed=True, unreachable_commit=commit,
                limits='Structural access only; signing, hooks and arbitrary external writes remain unverified. The unreachable probe commit remains for normal Git pruning.')


def codex_args(manifest, mode):
    digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    profile = 'varde_probe_' + digest
    table = '{' + ','.join(json.dumps(p) + '="write"' for p in manifest['writes']) + '}'
    overrides = ['-c', f'permissions.{profile}.extends=":workspace"',
                 '-c', f'permissions.{profile}.filesystem={table}']
    if mode == 'sandbox':
        return ['codex', 'sandbox', *overrides, '-P', profile, '-C', manifest['worktree'], '/usr/bin/true']
    return ['codex', 'exec', *overrides, '-c', 'default_permissions=' + json.dumps(profile),
            '-C', manifest['worktree']]


def sandbox_test(fixture_root):
    """Exercise actual write denial/grant outside nested seatbelt, no model call."""
    Path(fixture_root).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='varde-permissions-', dir=fixture_root) as fixture:
        parent = Path(fixture) / 'parent'
        worker = Path(fixture) / 'worker'
        git(fixture, 'init', str(parent))
        git(parent, '-c', 'user.name=Probe', '-c', 'user.email=probe@example.invalid',
            'commit', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'fixture')
        git(parent, 'worktree', 'add', '-b', 'worker', str(worker))
        m = describe(parent, worker, 'fixture', 'fixture', [])
        Path(m['approval_lock']).touch()  # Binding provisions the exact lock.
        # Full structural check within the child seatbelt; fixture has no
        # approval subject. The production check always runs the real gate.
        command = ['python3', '-B', '-c',
                   'import importlib.util,json; s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("p",' +
                   repr(str(Path(__file__).resolve())) +
                   '); p=importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(p); '
                   'print(json.dumps(p.check(json.loads(' + repr(json.dumps(m)) +
                   '),gate=lambda m:open(m["approval_lock"],"r+b").close())))']
        denied = subprocess.run(['codex', 'sandbox', '-c', 'permissions.varde_denial.extends=":workspace"',
                                 '-c', 'permissions.varde_denial.filesystem={}', '-P', 'varde_denial',
                                 '-C', str(worker), *command]).returncode
        allowed = subprocess.run(codex_args(m, 'sandbox')[:-1] + command).returncode
        if denied == 0 or allowed != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f'expected no-grant failure/grant success: {denied}/{allowed}')
        print(json.dumps({'no_grant_exit': denied, 'grant_exit': allowed}))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('command', choices=['describe', 'check', 'codex-args', 'sandbox-test'])
    parser.add_argument('--repository')
    parser.add_argument('--worktree')
    parser.add_argument('--subject')
    parser.add_argument('--binding')
    parser.add_argument('--write', action='append', default=[], metavar='EXTRA_VERIFICATION_DIR')
    parser.add_argument('--mode', choices=['sandbox', 'exec'], default='sandbox')
    parser.add_argument('--fixture-root')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == 'sandbox-test':
        sandbox_test(args.fixture_root)
        return
    if not all((args.repository, args.worktree, args.subject, args.binding)):
        parser.error('--repository, --worktree, --subject and --binding are required')
    manifest = describe(args.repository, args.worktree, args.subject, args.binding, args.write)
    result = manifest
    if args.command == 'check':
        result = check(manifest)
    elif args.command == 'codex-args':
        result = codex_args(manifest, args.mode)
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        main()
    except (OSError, RuntimeError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f'worktree permissions failed: {error}', file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
=== skills/varde-change/scripts/worktree-wave.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the deterministic steps of a worktree wave: start, integrate, publish, release.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF2'
Usage:
  worktree-wave.sh start <wave-id> <subject-id> <task-id>... \
      --scope <task-id>=<path>... [--task <task-id>=<abs-task-file>]...
  worktree-wave.sh integrate <wave-id> --check <command>
  worktree-wave.sh publish <wave-id> --approved <verified-commit>
  worktree-wave.sh release <wave-id>

Run from the clean, committed approval checkout (which may be a linked plan
worktree). The task id is also the binding id.

start      Records the physical approval checkout, branch, HEAD and tasks;
           creates fresh sibling workers and binds each to that checkout.
           Rerun an unfinished start with the same arguments to recover.
integrate  Merges workers in task-id order into a sibling integration tree,
           checks the combined result and prints its worktree, branch, base
           and verified_commit for IDE/Git review. Never moves the target.
           An unchanged verified result needs no repeated check.
publish    Requires explicit approval of the exact verified commit; validates
           clean, unchanged integration and workers and a clean target at
           the starting commit, then fast-forwards that target. Reruns are safe.
release    After publication, releases bindings and cleans up recovery refs.
           Record task transitions and commit bookkeeping before release.

Exit codes:
  0  success
  1  usage error or pending provisioning/release/cleanup step
  3  merge conflict; resolve and commit in the printed integration worktree,
     then rerun integrate (conflict hunks stay in IDE/Git tools)
  4  dirty, moved, stale, detached or missing checkout/ref; approval mismatch
  5  failed task or combined check (recovery refs kept)

EOF2
}

die() { echo "error: $1" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SELF="$(basename "$0")"

[[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]] && { usage; exit 0; }
[[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { usage >&2; exit 1; }
cmd="$1" wave="$2"; shift 2
git check-ref-format "refs/heads/worktree/${wave}-integration" || die "invalid wave id '${wave}'"

common="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"
repo="$(dirname "$common")"
state="$common/varde-waves/$wave"
integration="${wave}-integration"
iw="$repo/.varde/worktrees/$integration"

state_all() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$state"; }
state_get() { state_all "$1" | tail -n 1; }
branch_exists() { git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$1"; }
version_of() { python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["data"]["version"])'; }

load_state() {
  [[ -f "$state" ]] || die "no recorded wave '${wave}'; run start first"
  approval="$(state_get approval)"
  [[ "$(cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && pwd -P)" == "$approval" ]] || die "run from approval checkout ${approval}" 4
  subject="$(state_get subject)" target="$(state_get target)" base="$(state_get base)" tasks="$(state_get tasks)"
  [[ "$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD)" == "$target" ]] || die "run from the target branch ${target}" 4
}

# Create (or reuse) one task's worker worktree, then bind it. Run in an `if`,
# so each step returns explicitly.
provision() {
  local id="$1" out worker_path version bind=() s f
  worker_path="$repo/.varde/worktrees/$id"
  if ! branch_exists "worktree/$id"; then
    out="$("$HERE/worktree-create.sh" --fresh "$id" "$base")" || return 1
    worker_path="$(sed -n 's/^path=//p' <<<"$out")"
  fi
  [[ -d "$worker_path" && "$(git -C "$worker_path" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD)" == "worktree/$id" && "$(git -C "$worker_path" rev-parse HEAD)" == "$base" && -z "$(git -C "$worker_path" status --porcelain)" ]] || {
    echo "error: existing worker ${id} is not clean at the recorded base" >&2
    return 1
  }
  version="$(varde work review inspect --subject "$subject" --phase pre-edit --json | version_of)" || return 1
  for s in "${scopes[@]}"; do [[ "$s" == "${id}="* ]] && bind+=(--scope "${s#*=}"); done
  for f in "${files[@]:-}"; do [[ "$f" == "${id}="* ]] && bind+=(--task "${f#*=}"); done
  varde work review bind-worktree --subject "$subject" --binding "$id" \
    --expected-version "$version" --worktree "$worker_path" "${bind[@]}" --json >/dev/null || return 1
  echo "provisioned=$id" >> "$state"
  echo "task=$id worktree=$worker_path branch=worktree/$id binding=$id subject=$subject repository=$approval"
}

start() {
  local subject="${1:-}" ids=() scopes=() files=() id target base
  [[ -n "$subject" ]] || { usage >&2; exit 1; }
  shift
  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
      --scope) scopes+=("${2:?--scope needs task=path}"); shift 2 ;;
      --task) files+=("${2:?--task needs task=file}"); shift 2 ;;
      -*) usage >&2; exit 1 ;;
      *) ids+=("$1"); shift ;;
    esac
  done
  [[ ${#ids[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { usage >&2; exit 1; }
  for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
    printf '%s\n' "${scopes[@]:-}" | grep "^${id}=" >/dev/null || die "task ${id} needs --scope ${id}=<path>"
  done

  local sorted approval
  approval="$(cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && pwd -P)"
  sorted="$(printf '%s\n' "${ids[@]}" | sort | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')"
  if [[ -f "$state" ]]; then
    # Resume a partial start from the recorded state.
    [[ "$(state_get subject)" == "$subject" && "$(state_get tasks)" == "$sorted" ]] \
      || die "wave ${wave} was recorded with a different subject or task list"
    [[ "$(state_get approval)" == "$approval" ]] || die "run from recorded approval checkout" 4
    [[ -z "$(state_get started)" ]] || die "wave ${wave} already started"
    target="$(state_get target)" base="$(state_get base)"
    [[ "$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD)" == "$target" && "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" == "$base" && -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ]] || die "approval checkout is dirty, moved or on another branch" 4
  else
    [[ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ]] || die "target checkout is not clean" 4
    target="$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD)" || die "approval checkout must be on a branch" 4
    base="$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD)" || die "approval checkout needs a committed HEAD" 4
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$state")"
    printf 'subject=%s\napproval=%s\ntarget=%s\nbase=%s\ntasks=%s\n' "$subject" "$approval" "$target" "$base" "$sorted" > "$state"
  fi

  for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
    if grep -qx "provisioned=$id" "$state"; then
      echo "skip $id (already provisioned)"
      continue
    fi
    if ! provision "$id"; then
      {
        echo "error: provisioning ${id} failed; wave state kept at ${state}"
        echo "provisioned so far: $(sed -n 's/^provisioned=//p' "$state" | tr '\n' ' ')"
        echo "next: fix the cause, then rerun the same '${SELF} start ${wave} ...' to resume"
        echo "to abandon: release bindings, run worktree-cleanup.sh for each created task, then delete ${state}"
      } >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  echo "started=true" >> "$state"
}

# A verification record covers the exact integration tip and every worker tip.
# Dirty trees and wrong branches cannot inherit a successful check.
verification_snapshot() {
  local id worker_path tip
  [[ -d "$iw" && "$(git -C "$iw" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD)" == "worktree/$integration" && -z "$(git -C "$iw" status --porcelain)" ]] || return 1
  printf 'integration=%s\n' "$(git -C "$iw" rev-parse HEAD)"
  for id in $tasks; do
    worker_path="$repo/.varde/worktrees/$id"
    [[ -d "$worker_path" && "$(git -C "$worker_path" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD)" == "worktree/$id" && -z "$(git -C "$worker_path" status --porcelain)" ]] || return 1
    tip="$(git -C "$worker_path" rev-parse HEAD)" || return 1
    [[ "$tip" != "$base" ]] && git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base" "$tip" || return 1
    git -C "$iw" merge-base --is-ancestor "$tip" HEAD || return 1
    printf 'worker=%s=%s\n' "$id" "$tip"
  done
}

review_location() {
  echo "worktree=$iw"
  echo "branch=worktree/$integration"
  echo "base=$base"
  echo "verified_commit=$(git -C "$iw" rev-parse HEAD)"
  echo "pending: review in IDE/Git, then ${SELF} publish ${wave} --approved $(git -C "$iw" rev-parse HEAD)"
}

integrate() {
  [[ $# == 2 && "${1:-}" == "--check" && -n "${2:-}" ]] || { usage >&2; exit 1; }
  local check="$2" id tip rc=0 snapshot after
  load_state
  [[ -n "$(state_get started)" ]] || die "wave ${wave} did not finish start; rerun start to resume"
  [[ -z "$(state_get published)" ]] || die "wave already published; record bookkeeping and release"
  if branch_exists "worktree/$integration"; then
    [[ -d "$iw" ]] || die "integration worktree ${iw} is missing; recover it before retrying" 4
  else
    "$HERE/worktree-create.sh" --fresh "$integration" "$base" >/dev/null
  fi

  if snapshot="$(verification_snapshot)" && [[ -f "$state.verified" && -f "$state.check" && "$(cat "$state.verified")" == "$snapshot" ]] && cmp -s "$state.check" <(printf '%s' "$check"); then
    review_location
    return
  fi
  rm -f "$state.verified" "$state.check"
  if git -C "$iw" rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD >/dev/null; then
    die "merge in ${iw} is unresolved; resolve and commit there, then rerun integrate" 3
  fi
  [[ "$(git -C "$iw" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD)" == "worktree/$integration" && -z "$(git -C "$iw" status --porcelain)" ]] || die "integration checkout is dirty or on another branch" 4
  for id in $tasks; do
    tip="$(git rev-parse --verify "worktree/$id^{commit}")" || die "branch worktree/${id} is missing" 4
    [[ -d "$repo/.varde/worktrees/$id" && -z "$(git -C "$repo/.varde/worktrees/$id" status --porcelain)" ]] || die "task ${id} has uncommitted changes or a missing worktree" 5
    [[ "$(git -C "$repo/.varde/worktrees/$id" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD)" == "worktree/$id" ]] || die "worker ${id} is on another branch" 4
    git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base" "$tip" || die "task ${id} no longer descends from the wave base" 4
    if [[ "$tip" != "$base" ]] && git -C "$iw" merge-base --is-ancestor "$tip" HEAD; then
      echo "skip $id (already integrated)"
      continue
    fi
    rc=0
    (cd "$iw" && "$HERE/worktree-merge.sh" "$id") || rc=$?
    case "$rc" in
      0) ;;
      3) die "conflict merging ${id}; resolve and commit in ${iw}, then rerun integrate" 3 ;;
      2|5) die "task ${id} failed (exit ${rc}); no merge was recorded for it" 5 ;;
      *) die "merging ${id} failed (exit ${rc})" ;;
    esac
  done
  snapshot="$(verification_snapshot)" || die "integration or worker changed before verification" 4
  (cd "$iw" && bash -c "$check") || die "combined check failed; refs kept" 5
  after="$(verification_snapshot)" || die "check changed integration or workers; refs kept" 4
  [[ "$snapshot" == "$after" ]] || die "integration or worker tip changed during check; rerun integrate" 4
  printf '%s' "$check" > "$state.check"
  printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" > "$state.verified"
  review_location
}

publish() {
  [[ $# == 2 && "${1:-}" == --approved && -n "${2:-}" ]] || { usage >&2; exit 1; }
  local approved="$2" snapshot tip
  load_state
  [[ -f "$state.verified" ]] || die "no successful combined check; run integrate first" 4
  snapshot="$(verification_snapshot)" || die "integration or worker is dirty, moved or missing; refs kept" 4
  [[ "$(cat "$state.verified")" == "$snapshot" ]] || die "verification is stale; rerun integrate" 4
  tip="$(git -C "$iw" rev-parse HEAD)"
  [[ "$approved" == "$tip" ]] || die "approval must name the exact verified commit ${tip}" 4
  [[ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ]] || die "approval checkout is dirty; refs kept" 4
  if [[ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" == "$tip" ]]; then
    echo "target already contains the approved integration commit"
  else
    [[ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" == "$base" ]] || die "target moved from ${base}; refs kept" 4
    git merge --ff-only "$tip" || die "cannot fast-forward ${target}; refs kept" 4
  fi
  [[ "$(state_get published)" == "$tip" ]] || echo "published=$tip" >> "$state"
  echo "published wave ${wave} into ${target} at ${tip}"
  echo "pending: record task transitions, commit bookkeeping, then run: ${SELF} release ${wave}"
}

release() {
  local id tip version pending=() released
  load_state
  [[ -n "$(state_get published)" ]] || die "wave is not published; review and publish before release"
  git merge-base --is-ancestor "$(state_get published)" HEAD || die "published integration is not in target; refs kept" 4
  released="$(state_all released)"
  for id in $tasks; do
    grep -qx "$id" <<<"$released" && continue
    if ! tip="$(git rev-parse --verify "worktree/$id^{commit}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
      pending+=("worktree/$id is missing; cannot release ${id}"); continue
    fi
    if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$tip" HEAD; then
      pending+=("${id} is not integrated into ${target}; integrate first"); continue
    fi
    if version="$(varde work review inspect-worktree --subject "$subject" --binding "$id" --json | version_of)" &&
       varde work review release-worktree --subject "$subject" --binding "$id" \
         --expected-version "$version" --commit "$tip" --json >/dev/null; then
      echo "released=$id" >> "$state"
    else
      pending+=("release binding ${id}")
    fi
  done
  report_pending "${pending[@]:-}"

  for id in $tasks "$integration"; do
    branch_exists "worktree/$id" || continue
    "$HERE/worktree-cleanup.sh" "$id" || pending+=("clean up worktree/${id}")
  done
  report_pending "${pending[@]:-}"
  rm -f "$state" "$state.verified" "$state.check"
  echo "released and cleaned up wave ${wave}"
}

report_pending() {
  [[ -n "${1:-}" ]] || return 0
  echo "pending (refs kept; fix, then rerun: ${SELF} release ${wave}):" >&2
  printf '  - %s\n' "$@" >&2
  exit 1
}

case "$cmd" in
  start|integrate|publish|release) "$cmd" "$@" ;;
  *) usage >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
=== skills/varde-docs/SKILL.md ===
---
name: varde-docs
description: "Refresh README.md, docs/*.md, and changelogs or release notes against current code, or regenerate domain specs from source. Not for agent instructions like SKILL.md or AGENTS.md."
---

# Maintain project documentation

Before editing any file, apply `references/review-gates.md` unless a caller's
approved gate already covers the edits, and carry its verdict to completion.

## Choose the reference

| Document type | Read |
|---|---|
